title: I Enforced the Coworking Hot-Desk Tag on the Founder Who Sat in Mine

parts.text: I scanned into Bay 12 at 8:41 a.m. and found the founder's hoodie on my tagged monitor arm. The house rule, printed by him, said tags beat vibes. I was twenty-eight, freelance PM, holding a laptop that needed the dual screens I paid the premium for. Nico said he was taking a customer call and I could sit on the couch. The couch is for podcasts. I photographed the tag, the hoodie, and the rule poster with his face. Then I wheeled the monitor arm two inches so the camera would show the tag in his Zoom background. At 8:47 his customer asked whose name was on the yellow tag behind his head.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The customer can read my name on the tag in his Zoom background.

social.video_title: The founder sat in my tagged bay on a customer call — Part 1/2
social.description: Premium screens, hoodie, a poster with his face. Zoom had the yellow tag. Would you have wheeled the arm?

parts.text: Nico laughed on the call and moved. Community Slack posted a reminder he wrote: TAGS BEAT VIBES. I sat in Bay 12. The hoodie went to lost and found, which is a milk crate. Membership billed him a day-pass for the untagged hour because the system is petty in a way I respect. I plugged in. Dual screens came back. Vibes did not beat the tag. The couch remained for podcasts.

social.description: His own Slack reminder, a milk-crate lost and found. Was a customer call a tag?
